name: Ian Browne

education.notes: School and degree not disclosed in public sources reviewed. ThinkBusiness interview only states he worked in Big Pharma in London prior to founding.

keyDecisions: Took a corporate Big Pharma role in London before founding — built healthcare-domain credibility from inside the industry.
lessons: A first job inside the industry you later disrupt is a legitimate substitute for a tech or VC CV — especially in regulated verticals like healthcare.
careerSteps.notes: Per ThinkBusiness interview Browne 'worked in Big Pharma in London' before founding My Surgery Website. Specific employer and dates not disclosed publicly.

keyDecisions: Founded a healthcare SaaS (websites + patient tools for GP surgeries) with a colleague rather than going further up the pharma career ladder.
Targeted a fragmented, software-underserved buyer (UK & Ireland GP practices) where willingness-to-pay was small but recurring and defensible.
Scaled to ~4,000–5,000 GP-surgery customers and millions of patient users across the UK & Ireland before exiting.
lessons: Healthcare SaaS into a fragmented buyer base can compound to a multi-thousand-customer book without needing a global hub.
A small geography is not a barrier if your buyers are also distributed (every GP practice is its own buyer).
careerSteps.notes: MedTech SaaS serving GP surgeries. Per multiple sources reached ~4,000–5,000 customer practices and millions of patient users before being acquired by NASDAQ-listed Stericycle. Exact founding year, exit year and exit value not publicly disclosed. UK Companies House lists 'MY SURGERY WEBSITE LIMITED' (07214802) as the corporate entity.

keyDecisions: Post-exit, returned to Northern Ireland and helped set up Ignite (Belfast accelerator) rather than relocating to London / starting a second venture.
Optimised for ecosystem leverage — supported NI founders who collectively raised over £100m in venture capital.
lessons: Post-exit, building local founder infrastructure compounds the next generation rather than competing with it.
In a small ecosystem an exited founder who stays disproportionately shapes the next cohort.
careerSteps.notes: Helped establish Ignite (Belfast-based pre-seed accelerator) supporting NI founders. Per ThinkBusiness, founders in the programme raised ~£100m collectively.

keyDecisions: Took the NDRC MD role running a 5-year, €17m all-island Irish accelerator across Dogpatch Labs, Portershed Galway, Republic of Work Cork, RDI Hub Kerry.
lessons: An exited founder is highly hireable into national ecosystem-leadership roles — operator credibility transfers to programme leadership.
careerSteps.notes: NDRC accelerator is contracted at €17m over 5 years across a network of innovation hubs.

keyDecisions: Building Founder Labs — a NI-based programme helping founders 'build, sell, scale and raise' with global ambition.
Continues to be NI-based rather than relocating after exit / ecosystem roles.
lessons: A career can layer founder → ecosystem-builder → second founder of ecosystem infrastructure itself.
Geographic loyalty is a viable career thesis — staying somewhere compounds soft power that relocating burns.
careerSteps.notes: Current role per LinkedIn / RocketReach: CEO, Founder Labs (Belfast). Programme positioning per landing page: 'global ambition from Northern Ireland.'

exitEvents.notes: My Surgery Website acquired by NASDAQ-listed Stericycle. Year and value not publicly disclosed in sources reviewed.

outcomes.currentStatus: Belfast-based ecosystem builder. CEO of Founder Labs; previously MD of NDRC; co-founder of Ignite NI.

lessons.lesson: You can build a real outcome from Northern Ireland if your buyer base is also distributed (e.g. GP surgeries across UK & Ireland).
lessons.source: Inferred from My Surgery Website trajectory — ThinkBusiness interview.

lessons.lesson: Big Pharma → healthcare-SaaS founder is a credible NI-to-exit path; domain expertise can substitute for tech-hub access.
Post-exit, ecosystem-building in your home region (Ignite NI, NDRC, Founder Labs) can be higher impact than the next venture — and is itself a multi-decade career.
lessons.source: Trajectory across Ignite NI, NDRC, Founder Labs.

notes: Load-bearing role model for the 'is NI viable?' question. Public data is thin on exact dates and exit value — the strongest verified facts are: Big Pharma London → founded My Surgery Website (UK & Ireland GP SaaS) → acquired by NASDAQ-listed Stericycle → returned to NI → Ignite NI co-founder → NDRC MD → Founder Labs CEO. Era: mid-2000s/early-2010s SaaS founder, now in an Altman-era ecosystem-builder phase.
